about: What the smallest desktop application loads (B3; omui-devtools check size --native): example 01 built as dist builds it (-O3, NDEBUG) with its symbol table kept, the allocated sections of its program counted (.bss and the symbols left out). Bytes.

budgets.why: 18,519,893 B (2026-11-18, GCC 16 on Linux x64, the world `full`). It was 18,473,342 B before the program could be composed: the 46 KB more is what being able to leave things out costs the default — mlibs.compose's run time (about 10 KiB) and three seams (the accessibility service, the GPU path with effects, the agent surface; 6–11 KB each) — accepted in review; `lean` is 15,178 KiB for it. Code 14.1 MB, data 4.0 MB — std 10.7%, SDL 7.9%, omui.ui.base 7.6%, omui.view 5.7%. The plan's bound after B1 (unreached code not linked: 26.7 MB before); what brings it down is in the compose design §13.2

installs_why: The providers the program installs (mlibs.compose): its world, `full`, held as the links are.
links_why: The packages built into the program (B5): a change to this list is a change to what the smallest application carries, said in review. Owed cuts: the image decoders (mcpplibs.mwrap.libjpeg_turbo, .libpng, .libwebp; compat.libpng, compat.libwebp, compat.zlib) reached through the view's Image and the agent's screenshots, and the solver (mlibs.dynamics, mlibs.simulation) through hanim — each to become its owner's feature (B6)
